diagnostic_evidence.quote: Throughout the paper, we let $\mF_t = \sigma(\{\xi_i\}_{i=0}^t)$, for any $t\geq 0$, be the filtration~of~$\sigma$-algebras generated by the sample sequence $\xi_0, \xi_1,\xi_2\ldots$.

issues.failure_explanation: Because each iterate uses past sketch matrices, neither $\bx_t$ nor generally $B_t$ is measurable with respect to the sample-only sigma-field $\mF_{t-1}$. Consequently quantities such as $\nabla F_t$ cannot be pulled out of conditional expectations as done in the convergence proof, and the claimed conditional-unbiasedness and martingale-difference properties used throughout the later analysis are not valid relative to the stated filtration.

failure_location.quote: Then, we take expectation on both sides conditioning on $\mF_{t-1}$ and obtain

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the filtration to include all past sketching and stepsize randomness, specify that the current sample and sketches are conditionally independent of that enlarged history, and consistently redo the conditional expectations with the correct pre-iteration sigma-fields.
issues.overall_effect: The conditional-expectation, martingale, convergence, normality, and covariance-estimation arguments are not formally established under the probability filtration defined in the paper.
issues.title: The filtration omits sketching randomness on which the iterates depend
issues.why_classification: This is a pervasive but standard filtration repair; the source's intended independence structure appears sufficient to preserve the claims once the history is defined correctly.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Furthermore, there exist constants $C_{g,1}, C_{g,2}>0$ such that

issues.failure_explanation: The assumptions impose only an upper moment bound and do not require the gradient-noise covariance, $\Omega^\star$, or $\Xi^\star$ to be positive definite. Thus $\hat\Xi_t^{-1}$ need not exist and a $d$-degree-of-freedom chi-square limit is not justified in singular cases. The assertion for every direction is also false for $\bw=0$: the displayed interval is always $[0,0]$ and has coverage one, not $1-q$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume $\Xi^\star$ is positive definite for the confidence region, restrict the interval claim to nonzero directions with $\bw^T\Xi^\star\bw>0$, and define the region only when the estimated covariance is invertible.
issues.overall_effect: The confidence-region conclusion and the directional confidence-interval conclusion fail for degenerate noise and zero-variance directions, regimes allowed by all stated assumptions.
issues.title: Confidence regions and intervals lack required covariance nondegeneracy
issues.why_classification: Adding standard nondegeneracy conditions and excluding zero-variance directions is a local restriction that preserves the inference result in its ordinary full-rank regime.

issues.failure_explanation: The recursion requires an already existing $\hat\Xi_t^{-1}$, but $\hat\Xi_0=0$. More generally, the centered covariance of $t$ vectors has rank at most $t-1$, so it is necessarily singular for $t\le d$. The paper gives no valid starting index or method for obtaining the first inverse. In addition, the main-text matrix $\Pi_t$ does not match the $\Lambda_t^{-1}$ derived in the appendix: the latter has first entry $-a_t$, not $a_t$.

failure_location.quote: for confidence region, $\hat{\Xi}_t^{-1}$ can also be updated online:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify an initialization after enough samples and compute one valid initial inverse, or introduce and analyze a regularized or pseudoinverse update; also replace the inconsistent $a_t$ sign in the main-text update.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted fully online, factorization-free construction of confidence-region inverses is not an executable recursion as written; the interval estimator itself is unaffected.
issues.title: The online inverse recursion cannot be initialized from the singular sample covariance
issues.why_classification: A complete repair either requires a nontrivial generalized-inverse or regularization construction, or sacrifices the advertised absence of matrix factorization by computing an initial full inverse.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Under the conditions in Lemma \ref{sec4:lem1}, except for strengthening $\chi>\beta$ to $\chi>1.5\beta$

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem sec4:thm1 explicitly inherits Lemma sec4:lem1, whose $B_t$ is the average of stochastic Hessians and whose proof establishes convergence to $B^\star=\nabla^2F(\bx^\star)$. Its decomposition and error estimates repeatedly use precisely that convergence. It therefore does not directly cover arbitrary conditioning matrices such as those used by AdaGrad, RMSProp, or quasi-Newton methods.

failure_location.quote: Notably, Theorem \ref{sec4:thm1} does~not~\mbox{require}~$B_t$~to~\mbox{converge}~to~the true Hessian $\nabla^2 F(\tx)$, making our analysis directly applicable to conditioned SGD methods.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must formulate assumptions for a general limiting conditioning matrix, derive the corresponding limiting covariance, and reprove the iterate decomposition and covariance-estimator bounds, or withdraw the direct-applicability claim.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised generalization of the covariance estimator's consistency and rate analysis to conditioned SGD is unsupported; the theorem remains limited to the Hessian-average sketched Newton setting.
issues.title: Claimed direct applicability to conditioned SGD contradicts the theorem's Hessian-average assumptions
issues.why_classification: The existing theorem proves the opposite structural premise, and preserving the claimed generality requires a new convergence and covariance analysis; otherwise the substantive generalization must be abandoned.
